acceptanceCriteria: The dogfood wrappers reuse a previously built current-tree corvint binary when a recorded input key (build-input tree digest, VERSION, Go version) matches and those paths are clean, and rebuild otherwise; DCW-V0-022 current-tree identity is preserved and the spec is updated in the same change.
A dirty or changed build input always forces a rebuild (test retained).
Measured: a second `make dogfood-change BASE=<sha>` on an unchanged tree skips the build, with before/after wall times retained.
body: Evidence: owner-requested performance search on 2026-10-17. Measured with corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 615, corvint-tasks build 615, Go 1.27.2, macOS 12-core/64 GB host at load average 80-84 (wall times are inflated by load; CPU times are the stable signal). Lane counts come from orchestrator session 03e2afac subagent transcripts (206 lanes). script/dogfood-change.sh, dogfood-check.sh, dogfood-finish.sh, dogfood-batch-check.sh and dogfood-bind-range.sh each run `go build -o $git_dir/corvint/corvint ./cmd/corvint` unless CORVINT_BIN is set. Measured in a clean worktree at origin/main c92ee0015: cold build 56.85 s wall (24.8 s user), immediate rebuild of the identical tree 16.37 s wall (1.1 s user), byte-identical output. Lanes ran dogfood-change 855 times, check 226, seal 179 and finish 152; at the 16 s warm floor that is at least 6 h of lane time spent relinking an unchanged binary. Expected: the wrapper reuses the previously built binary when the build inputs are unchanged (for example keyed by the Git tree digest of the build inputs plus go.sum, VERSION and GOVERSION, with a clean-worktree check for those paths), and rebuilds otherwise. Distinct from V1-1629, which reduces how often lanes run dogfood at all.
title: dogfood wrappers rebuild cmd/corvint on every invocation: 16 s warm, 57 s cold, about 1,400 lane invocations
